data.raw_text:
WTF?! Permission Required from the Americans to Use EDCA Sites, even in a State of Emergency? Seriously?!

This is beyond frustrating. We’re facing severe flooding in Metro Manila and surrounding areas, as well as other areas of the country. Yet, we still have to ask permission from the Americans to access EDCA (Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement) sites for disaster response and relief operations. 

Hell! That’s an outrage. To add insult to injury, it’s only now that the so-called “man from Malta” finally decided to coordinate, when things are already spiraling out of control. Goodness gracious!

WTF!! Have we effectively surrendered our sovereignty? Imagine that: in our own land, we must seek approval from the Kano (Americans) to mobilize EDCA sites for relief operations?! Nakakagalit! Infuriating doesn’t even begin to describe it.

Folks, this is precisely what I’ve been harping on about. This is what I am always emphasizing. Insofar as EDCA sites are concerned, there’s such a thing as Operational Bottlenecks. The effective deployment depends heavily on legal-clearance mechanisms, infrastructure readiness, and diplomatic coordination. As previously seen, legal and administrative delays can hinder the timeliness of relief and rescue efforts. In short, PH is NOT in full control, and that’s a dangerous flaw when lives are on the line.

It’s the same problem with the Mutual Defense Treaty (MDT) between the U.S. and the Philippines. It’s not a magical security blanket. The MDT doesn’t guarantee automatic assistance, because any response from the U.S. hinges on whether it serves American national interests at that moment. Not Philippine interests. Their interests.

Oh, and let’s not forget: there’s no “instant retaliation clause in the MDT.” If the Philippines is attacked, the U.S. president still needs to ask Congress for permission before doing anything, so much for ironclad guarantees.

Goodness gracious! Wake up, Philippines! We’ve turned ourselves into a tenant in our own house, and worse, we can’t even get emergency help without clearing it with the landlord.

The absence of integrated urban planning for the NCR is the reason for what we go through when the rainy season comes. 

How long will we put up with this? The NCR obviously needs a Governor to oversee the needs of its residents and transients with the authority over the Mayors who have their own fiefdom. 

Will we wait for the time when the whole NCR  is submerged in floodwaters before we finally see the light? 

All president's post-martial law have never brought up the need to bring back the post of Governor. The last governor of Metro Manila was Imelda Marcos. 

At least she had a vision for what she referred to then as the city of man. Most of the infrastructure she built has stood the test of time, specially the hospitals. 

As it is now, god is our last resort in times of natural disasters but the flooding we go through is our fault because of the lack of planning. 

When will we ever learn?
